title: Radix pass counting-sort preconditions
statement: Let $L$ have word bound $L.word$, space bound $L.space$, and depth bound $L.depth$; let $\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be a memory map, let $A$ be radix-pass arguments, let $\pi$ be a list of natural numbers, and let $kd:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $L.space\le L.word$, $|\pi|=A.w$, every entry of $\pi$ is less than $A.w$, and the entries of $\pi$ are stored consecutively starting at $A.perm$. For every $i<A.w$, suppose the key cell $A.key+i\cdot A.stride+A.off$ lies before $A.perm$, stores $kd(i)$, and $kd(i)<A.nb$; also suppose $A.perm+2A.w\le A.cnt$, $A.cnt+(A.nb+1)\le A.perm+A.R$, and $A.perm+A.R\le L.space$. Then the counting-sort arguments with $A.w$ items, source address $A.perm$, destination address $A.perm+A.w$, and the same key parameters, key bound, and counter address satisfy the counting-sort preconditions: item $j$ is the entry of $\pi$ at position $j$, or $0$ if $j\ge|\pi|$, and its key is $kd$ of that item. In particular, the source, destination, and counter regions fit in memory and are pairwise disjoint; each item key cell fits in memory, lies outside the destination and counter regions, and stores a key less than $A.nb$; and the destination and counter regions fit in memory and are disjoint.
hypotheses_covered: Every entry of $\pi$ is less than $A.w$
$\pi$ is represented in memory starting at $A.perm$
For each $i<A.w$, the key cell address is before $A.perm$
For each $i<A.w$, that key cell stores $kd(i)$
replaced:
Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$, let
$w,\mathrm{perm},\mathrm{key},\mathrm{stride},\mathrm{off},\mathrm{nb},R\in\mathbb N$,
let $\pi$ be a list of natural numbers, and let $kd:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. Suppose the
memory and word bounds satisfy $\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$; the list has length $w$
and every entry is less than $w$; its entries occupy the consecutive cells beginning at
$\mathrm{perm}$; for every $i<w$, the key cell
$\mathrm{key}+i\,\mathrm{stride}+\mathrm{off}$ lies before $\mathrm{perm}$ and stores
$kd(i)<\mathrm{nb}$; and $\mathrm{perm}+2w\le\mathrm{cnt}$,
$\mathrm{cnt}+\mathrm{nb}+1\le\mathrm{perm}+R$, and $\mathrm{perm}+R\le\mathrm{space}$.
Then the counting-sort setup with $w$ items in cells beginning at $\mathrm{perm}$,
destination beginning at $\mathrm{perm}+w$, and the same key and counter parameters
satisfies its preconditions: item $j<w$ is the $j$th entry of $\pi$ (taken to be $0$ if
$j$ is out of range), its key is $kd$ of that item, every item and destination cell and
the counter region fit in memory, each key cell fits in memory and stores the specified
key below $\mathrm{nb}$, and the source, destination, counter, and key-cell regions are
disjoint as required.
